newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices fall sharply in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices fall sharply in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices fell at auction sales in Newcastle, Melbourne and Fremantle this week, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
The eastern market indicator fell 15 cents to 574 cents a kg clean, while the western indicator fell five cents to 520 cents.
A total of 96,927 bales were offered, with 13.2 percent passed in.
The council said price falls were greatest in the 20.5 micron and finer categories.
"Exporters report that demand from overseas processors is very subdued at present due to market conditons.

"Typically, wool processors restrain wool purchases when prices are falling, minimising stock holding and purchasing only what is required to meet commitments to spinners and weavers," the council said.
In the futures market, a total of 322 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended September 26.
Wool International said it sold 21,370 bales, leaving the stockpile at 2,071,840 bales.
Sales next week are in Sydney and Geelong with 69,566 bales on offer.
